rationale.correct: Step 1: Full-load cooling capacity = 200 TR × 12,000 BTU/hr × (70% load factor) = 1,680,000 BTU/hr effective = 492 kW. Step 2: Full-load input power at 4.8 COP = 492 kW ÷ 4.8 = 102.5 kW. Step 3: Annual operating hours = 10 hr/day × 250 days = 2,500 hr/year. Step 4: Annual energy = 102.5 kW × 2,500 hr = 256.25 MWh ≈ 256 MWh. Alternative approach: 200 TR = 200 × 3.517 kW = 703.4 kW input at full load; at 70% = 492.4 kW × 2,500 hr ÷ 4.8 COP adjustment is redundant; direct calculation: 492.4 kW × 2,500 = 1,231 MWh. Recalculating with proper approach: 200 TR × 12,000 BTU/hr = 2,400,000 BTU/hr = 703.4 kW cooling output at full load. At 70% load = 492.4 kW cooling output. Input = 492.4 ÷ 4.8 = 102.5 kW. Annual = 102.5 × 2,500 = 256.25 MWh. Source: ASHRAE energy calculation standards.
rationale.takeaway: Chiller annual energy estimation requires separating cooling output (TR × 12,000 BTU/hr) from electrical input (COP division), accounting for part-load utilization factor (70% in this case) representing typical office seasonal operation (lower load in cooler months, higher in peak summer).
